purpose: A moving, car-based loop through Ireland's south and west that puts scenic coastline, history and food at the centre of nearly every day, matching a traveller happy to cover ground and see the icons even when busy.
routeRationale: Fly into Dublin, cross to Kilkenny for early medieval/history texture, then run the classic southwest arc (Cork/Kinsale, Killarney/Ring of Kerry, Dingle) before heading up the Wild Atlantic Way to the Cliffs of Moher and Galway/Connemara, f
assumptions: One special meal reserved for Dingle or Kinsale, both noted foodie towns
Late night once in Dublin and once in Galway for music/pubs, never before an early departure day
No internal flights; all transfers by car and one short ferry-less coastal drive
tradeoffs: Skips Northern Ireland and the Giant's Causeway entirely to keep the south/west loop coherent in 10 days
Only one night added in Kilkenny rather than lingering, to protect time for Kerry and Clare
Connemara gets a day rather than a full base, since Galway city serves both the town and the peninsula within the drivin

bases.name: Dublin
bases.why: Arrival base close to the airport and city centre for an easy first evening.
bases.lodgingArea: Dublin city centre near Trinity/Temple Bar

bases.name: Kilkenny
bases.why: Compact medieval town on the drive south, good base for castle and historic centre.

bases.name: Kinsale
bases.why: Harbour town near Cork with excellent food scene, ideal first taste of the southwest coast.

bases.name: Killarney
bases.why: Best base for the Ring of Kerry loop and Killarney National Park without daily hotel moves.

bases.name: Dingle
bases.why: Own peninsula loop and lively pub-and-seafood town, worth a dedicated night rather than a day trip.

bases.name: Galway
bases.why: Central for Cliffs of Moher, the Burren and Connemara, plus a genuinely good city in its own right.
bases.lodgingArea: Galway city centre near the Latin Quarter

bases.name: Dublin
bases.why: Return to Dublin for the flight home; last night kept light before a morning departure.
bases.lodgingArea: Dublin city centre or near the airport

days.theme: Arrival and first taste of Dublin

anchors.name: Trinity College and the Book of Kells
anchors.why: Iconic first stop, manageable after an afternoon arrival.

anchors.name: Temple Bar and Grafton Street
anchors.why: Easy evening stroll to get oriented.

anchors.name: Traditional pub with live music
anchors.why: One late night fits well on arrival evening before a light travel day follows.

meals.dinner: Pub dinner in Temple Bar area

days.note: Keep this day unhurried given the afternoon arrival.
days.whyItFits: Delivers Dublin's core icon and neighbourhood life without overloading a jetlagged first evening.

anchors.name: Kilkenny Castle
anchors.why: Well-preserved castle and gardens, an easy anchor after the drive.

anchors.name: Medieval Mile and St Canice's Cathedral
anchors.why: Compact historic core, walkable at a relaxed pace.

days.note: Short relocation day, drive under two hours.
days.whyItFits: A gentle transfer day that still gives real history and a distinct town character.

days.theme: To the harbour town via Cork

anchors.name: Rock of Cashel
anchors.why: Dramatic ecclesiastical site directly on the route south, a must for history lovers.

anchors.name: English Market
anchors.why: Cork's celebrated food market fits the food-forward brief without a detour.

anchors.name: Charles Fort and harbour walk
anchors.why: Star fort with sea views, easy evening stop after checking in.

days.note: Longer relocation day but broken up by two worthwhile stops.
days.whyItFits: Combines a landmark historic site, a market for local food culture, and a coastal arrival.

anchors.name: Kinsale town walk and harbour
anchors.why: Morning stroll before departing, since the town rewards slow looking.

anchors.name: Killarney National Park and Muckross House
anchors.why: Lakes and woodland right at the new base, ideal after a driving day.

days.note: Moderate drive, arrive with the afternoon free for the park.
days.whyItFits: Balances a relocation with an easy nature walk rather than more driving.

anchors.name: Ladies View and Moll's Gap
anchors.why: Classic panoramic viewpoint on the loop.

anchors.name: Skellig Ring and Portmagee
anchors.why: Quieter, more dramatic alternative to the main Ring road, within the driving ceiling.

anchors.name: Kerry Cliffs
anchors.why: Sea cliffs rivalling Moher with far fewer people.

anchors.name: Killarney town pub dinner
anchors.why: Relaxed evening back at base after a full scenic day.

days.note: A full loop day; keep the car moving steadily to stay near the driving ceiling.
days.whyItFits: This is the scenic heart of the trip, a full day dedicated to the coastline and viewpoints.

anchors.name: Slea Head Drive
anchors.why: Iconic coastal loop with beehive huts and ocean views, the peninsula's signature drive.

anchors.name: Dunquin Pier and Blasket Islands view
anchors.why: Short stop with dramatic island views.

anchors.name: Dingle town and harbour
anchors.why: Colourful fishing town with a strong food and music scene.

meals.lunch: Packed lunch on Slea Head Drive

days.note: The trip's one special meal, in a town known nationally for its food scene.
days.whyItFits: Delivers a second, distinct scenic peninsula and reserves the special meal where it is best earned.

days.theme: Cliffs of Moher and the Burren en route to Galway

anchors.name: Cliffs of Moher
anchors.why: One of Ireland's defining landscapes, unmissable even with crowds.

anchors.name: The Burren
anchors.why: Otherworldly limestone landscape directly on the route north.

anchors.name: Galway Latin Quarter evening walk
anchors.why: Lively arrival evening with buskers and pubs.

days.note: A relocation day anchored by the trip's biggest single icon.
days.whyItFits: Puts the Cliffs of Moher and Burren in their natural place on the route, no detour needed.

anchors.name: Kylemore Abbey
anchors.why: Lakeside abbey and gardens, a classic Connemara stop.

anchors.name: Sky Road, Clifden
anchors.why: Loop drive with sweeping Atlantic views.

anchors.name: Galway city walk and pub session
anchors.why: Second late night, back at base after an outdoor day.

days.note: Loop day within the driving ceiling, returning to the same base.
days.whyItFits: Gives Connemara its own day without a hotel move, keeping scenery central.

days.theme: Cross-country to Dublin via the Midlands

anchors.name: Clonmacnoise monastic site
anchors.why: Significant early Christian ruins directly on the route east, adding depth to the history theme.

anchors.name: Dublin evening stroll and Guinness Storehouse area
anchors.why: A fitting last full evening covering Dublin's most famous export.

days.note: Longest relocation day, broken by one historic stop.
days.whyItFits: Uses the transfer day for a genuine history highlight rather than pure driving.

anchors.name: Local café and short walk near base
anchors.why: Morning departure allows only a short, unhurried walk before the airport.

days.note: Morning flight; nothing scheduled beyond a short walk.
days.whyItFits: Respects the hard departure window with a light close to the trip.

omissions.name: Giant's Causeway and Northern Ireland
omissions.reason: Adding the north would require either flying or extending driving well past the ceiling; the south/west loop stays coherent instead.

omissions.name: Aran Islands boat trip
omissions.reason: Would need a half-day ferry detour from Galway that competes with Connemara for the same day; Connemara chosen as the stronger scenic fit.

omissions.name: Full second day in Kilkenny
omissions.reason: One night keeps the pace toward the southwest and Kerry, the trip's scenic centre.

transport.summary: Self-drive loop by rental car from Dublin, southwest to Kerry and Dingle, up the Wild Atlantic Way to Clare and Galway, then back across the Midlands to Dublin; all legs stay within or near the 150-mi
notes: Irish roads are narrow on peninsulas like Dingle and the Ring of Kerry; allow extra time even for short distances
No ferries required in this route; the Aran Islands option was omitted partly for this reason
Return the car in Dublin before the final morning if the airport hotel is chosen for the last night

beforeYouGo: Check current entry requirements for the traveller's nationality
Confirm rental car insurance covers Irish roads and one-way drop-off in Dublin
Book the Dingle special dinner and any timed Cliffs of Moher tickets a few weeks ahead
packing: Waterproof jacket and layers, Irish weather changes quickly even in May
Comfortable walking shoes for cliff paths and cobbled towns
A daypack for packed lunches and layers on outdoor days

backups.trigger: Heavy rain or wind on the Ring of Kerry day
backups.alternative: Prioritise Ladies View and Kerry Cliffs early, shelter with a museum or distillery visit in Killarney town if conditions worsen

backups.trigger: Cliffs of Moher very crowded or weather closes the cliff path
backups.alternative: Substitute time at the Burren's Poulnabrone dolmen and Doolin village instead

backups.trigger: Kilkenny Castle or Kylemore Abbey fully booked
backups.alternative: Walk the surrounding gardens and grounds, which remain accessible without a ticket
